label: Nov 2–6, 2026
title: Alphabet’s cash burn and Intel’s plunge break the S&P 500’s 100-day line
deck: Alphabet fell 12.6% Thursday on $9.1B of negative free cash flow, and Intel had its worst day since 1974 on Friday. The S&P 500 fell 1.8% Friday to 7,580, its first close below the 100-day average since April, yet nine of 11 sectors rose on the week. Next: Apple Monday, the midterms and AMD Tuesday, and the October jobs report Friday.

tldr.label: What changed
tldr.text: Alphabet’s cash burn and Intel’s 29% drop pushed the S&P 500 below its 100-day line. Under the surface, nine of 11 sectors rose and the equal-weight index beat the S&P 500 for a third week.

tldr.label: What’s next
tldr.text: Apple and Palantir Monday, midterms and AMD Tuesday, jobs Friday (about 55K expected after 29K). December hike odds sit near 80–85% after two hawkish dissents.

tldr.label: Who’s buying
tldr.text: ARK bought Robinhood and Coinbase as they fell and sold Eli Lilly, TSMC and AMD. Rep. Sessions disclosed a Microsoft sale; Rep. Hern sold Seagate, Texas Instruments and ASML.

scorecard.call: Microsoft and Alphabet on Fed day
scorecard.outcome: Split. Microsoft’s Azure grew 48% and the stock gave up less than 2% over two days. Alphabet reported negative free cash flow of $9.1B on $51.4B of capex and fell 12.6% Thursday, despite Google Cloud revenue more than doubling.
Broke. The S&P 500 closed at 7,580.07 on Friday, its first close below the 100-day average since early April and its lowest close since Sept 16. The week’s low was 7,527.56.

September PCE came in at 3.6% as forecast, core at 3.1%. Front-month Brent settled at $117.64 Friday, a six-month high. The Fed held, with Cook and Hammack dissenting for a hike, and December hike odds rose to about 85%.

levels.name: S&P 500
levels.note: Lance Roberts notes Friday’s close landed below both the 100-day near 7,615 and the lower Bollinger band, with RSI dropping from 50.8 to 40.1 in one session. A close back above 7,615 would make Friday look like a one-day shakeout. First support is the Sept 16 close near 7,552, then the July 31 close near 7,490; below that, he would tighten stops, with the 200-day near 7,310.

sectors.title: Big Tech sank, the rest of the market rose
sectors.deck: Nine of 11 sectors rose. Communication services fell 5.3% on Alphabet and tech fell 2.0% on Intel; health care led with a 3.1% gain and materials rose 2.8%.

flows.label: Equal-weight vs S&P 500
flows.note: A third straight week of the average stock beating the megacaps. The Russell 2000 rose 1.3%.

flows.label: Growth vs value since Oct 7
flows.note: Per the Bull Bear Report, 17 sessions of growth losing to value pushed the ratio’s RSI to 28.6, below the 30 level usually read as washed out.

flows.label: Stretch vs the S&P 500
flows.note: Relative to their 50-day averages, energy, health care and staples are the most overbought; communications (−8.4%) and tech are the most oversold.

flows.label: Chip stocks
flows.note: Most of the damage came Friday: the VanEck semiconductor ETF fell 7.9% that day as Intel dropped 29% and AMD 12%.

sectors.takeaway: Money left the AI spenders and their suppliers and spread into everything else. Apple, AMD and Qualcomm this week will test whether that rotation keeps running.

big_money.lag_note: Congress has up to 45 days to report a trade, and Trump’s monthly reports arrive about six weeks after the month ends. Fund trades like ARK’s are published daily. These show what they bought, not what they’re buying today.

news.headline: Alphabet joined Meta in the cash-burn club
news.body: Alphabet reported negative free cash flow of $9.1B on $51.4B of quarterly capex and fell 12.6% Thursday, a one-day loss of about $497B in market value. Google Cloud revenue more than doubled. Amazon’s AWS grew 39% but earnings missed; Microsoft’s Azure grew 48% and the stock barely moved.

news.headline: Intel had its worst day since 1974
news.body: Intel fell about 29% Friday after a weak fourth-quarter forecast, citing a PC slump and a factory accident in Israel. Reddit also fell about 29% and Twilio 17%. AMD fell 12% and Nvidia 5%, and the Nasdaq lost 2.9%, its worst day since June.

news.headline: The Fed held, two voted to hike
news.body: Rates stayed at 3.75–4.00% in a 10–2 vote, with Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissenting for a hike. September PCE inflation was 3.6% and core 3.1%; Q3 GDP grew 3.4% and wage growth slowed to 3.1%.

news.headline: A $6.3B hack hit Binance
news.body: Attackers took about $6.3B on Thursday, including 18,270 BTC; about $3B is frozen and Binance says it will cover losses. It paused withdrawals, aimed to resume them in phases by Sunday and plans a proof-of-reserves report Monday. Coinbase fell 10.6% and Strategy 7.8% Friday.

news.headline: Iran talks continue as strike talk grows
news.body: Iranian officials met Qatari mediators in Doha over a plan to reopen Hormuz. Trump said talks were going fine but not very reliable, and that the US still had sites to take care of. The US reportedly warned Gulf allies of a short, intense round after Tuesday’s midterms; Iran’s supreme leader promised an immediate response.

news.headline: Oil at six-month highs; OPEC+ stood pat
news.body: Front-month Brent settled at $117.64 Friday and WTI at $104.12, a fourth straight monthly gain, after at least 35 attacks on ships in October. On Sunday OPEC+ kept December output targets unchanged; most members are producing below target because of the war.

news.headline: Midterms on Tuesday
news.body: All 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats are up. Polymarket odds cited in the Bull Bear Report were about 94% for Democrats taking the House and 69% for the Senate.

calendar.title: Apple, Palantir, ISM manufacturing
calendar.body: ISM manufacturing, with Fed’s Goolsbee speaking. Marriott before the open; Apple, Palantir and Vertex after. Binance plans its proof-of-reserves report.

calendar.title: Midterm elections, AMD
calendar.body: Election Day. JOLTS job openings and factory orders. Shopify and Pfizer before the open; AMD, Amgen, Arista and Booking after.

calendar.title: ISM services, Qualcomm, Uber
calendar.body: ISM services, ADP jobs and the Treasury’s quarterly refunding. Uber, CVS and Datadog before the open; Qualcomm, Arm, AppLovin and DoorDash after.

calendar.title: Airbnb, Bank of England
calendar.body: Jobless claims, Q3 productivity and Challenger job cuts; Fed’s Hammack speaks. Bank of England decides. ConocoPhillips and Cigna before the open; Airbnb and Cloudflare after.

calendar.title: October jobs report
calendar.body: Payrolls at 8:30am ET, plus University of Michigan sentiment. A soft number with inflation at 3.6% would test December hike bets.

consensus_note: Payroll and wage consensus via Tech Insider (CNBC and KPMG forecasts, range 45K–65K); ISM consensus from the Bull Bear Report, prior from PNC. December hike odds are futures pricing: about 85% per the Bull Bear Report and about 80% per Reuters’ week-ahead column.
further: Further out: Q3 13F filings from Berkshire, Pershing Square and other funds in mid-November, and the next Fed meeting in December.

crypto.headline: Bitcoin lost $80K after the Binance hack
crypto.deck: Spot ETFs took in about $441M over four days, then lost $643M on Friday after the hack, leaving the week about $202M negative. Bitcoin touched $76,141 Friday, its lowest since Sept 17, and was near $78K on Sunday.

stats.label: Spot ETF net flow, Oct 26–30
stats.note: Friday’s $643M exit was led by BlackRock’s IBIT (−$234M), Fidelity’s FBTC (−$201M) and ARK’s ARKB (−$130M).

stats.label: What drives it this week
stats.note: Binance’s withdrawal restart and Monday proof-of-reserves report, the midterms, and Friday’s jobs data.

crypto.signal: Reclaiming $80K, then the $81.5K–82.5K supply zone, would ease the pressure. A daily close below the $74.9K–76K support band could open $72K, per CoinCentral.

bottom_line.title: Apple and AMD after Alphabet
bottom_line.body: Investors rewarded Microsoft, whose cash flow covers its AI spending, and punished Meta and Alphabet, whose didn’t. Apple Monday and AMD Tuesday face the same test of spending versus cash.

bottom_line.title: The 7,615 line, now overhead
bottom_line.body: A close back above the 100-day near 7,615 would make Friday a shakeout. Below the Sept 16 close near 7,552, the next marks are 7,490 and then the 200-day near 7,310.

bottom_line.title: Midterms, then jobs
bottom_line.body: The election lands Tuesday amid reports of possible Iran strikes afterward. Friday’s jobs report is expected near 55K; a soft print with 3.6% inflation would test December hike odds near 80–85%.
